name: Strasserism
summary: Strasserism is the 'German socialism' of Otto Strasser and, in the 1925/26 programme, of his brother Gregor: a dissident current of National Socialism that broke with Hitler in 1930. It makes the nation the sole owner of land, raw materials and the means of production, which individuals and 'factory fellowships' of manager, workers and State hold in hereditary fief, and replaces parties and parliament with vocational councils and Chambers of Estates under a president elected for life, in a federal Germany of provinces. It rejects Marxism, class struggle, capitalism and the totalitarian State alike; its early programme excluded Jews from citizenship, while Strasser's later writings proposed minority rights and a European federation.
scope: Otto Strasser's doctrine as the defining sources tie it to him: the 1925/26 Strasser programme (Kühnl, s8, s9), the Aufbau des deutschen Sozialismus of 1931 and 1936 with the Black Front's manifestos, reprinted with Strasser's 1940 peace proposals in Germany Tomorrow (s7), as treated by Gottfried (s10) and Hughes (s11). The Aufbau, held and republished from 1931 to 1940, is taken as the mature position; where the 1925/26 draft (withdrawn in 1926) or the 1940 proposals differ, the answer records the change. Hitler and I (s1) is used sparingly, as historians doubt its self-portrait. Gregor Strasser's separate 1932 positions and the neo-Strasserism of later groups are other subjects and are excluded.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Germany Tomorrow keeps a national militia or a composite European army.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The Aufbau makes the Reichsbank a State institution that issues notes and sets the official interest rate, and demands a national currency standard of its own.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Aufbau demands equality of opportunity with no handicaps in life, rejects hereditary monarchy and gives the new elite a title acquired by personal choice, not birth.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: The Aufbau abolishes the existing scale and method of taxation in favour of tithes, imposts and guild lump sums, leaving the inheritance tax and a few luxury taxes as the only old taxes.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: German socialism keeps money, wages suited to each worker's achievement and interest on loans, and only removes private ownership of monopoly goods.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: Workers in the factory fellowship receive wages suited to their achievements besides a small profit share, so wage labour remains.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The Aufbau wants machinery made a servant again and rejects the liberal ideal of boundless production.

alienated-labor.rationale: The Aufbau condemns industrial work's murderous monotony and the proletarian character of life, and wants daily toil to take only a fraction of life so the worker finds room for creation.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: The Aufbau says the land available for the community is owned exclusively by the nation, whose organizational form is the State, and is only leased out in entail.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Germany Tomorrow calls the Munich agreement extorted by force and demands evacuation of all occupied non-German areas and cancellation of Hitler's conquest of Austria.

apologise-for-past-wrongs.rationale: Germany Tomorrow says Germany must atone for its complicity in Hitler's violence, repudiate it on principle and pay reparations to Poland and Czechoslovakia.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The 1940 programme makes freedom of belief and conscience a foundation of the New Germany and the Aufbau proclaims freedom of faith and conscience.

arbitrator-settles-disputes.rationale: Germany Tomorrow requires every member of the European Federation to recognise its arbitral powers and the Permanent Court of International Justice.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Aufbau says the violent act is the end, not the beginning, of a revolution that first transforms Germans' feelings and will.

arms-reduction.rationale: Germany Tomorrow calls a general agreement to disarm, reducing armaments to a modest fraction under reciprocal control, the most decisive guarantee of security.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Strasser's 1940 programme lets members of other stocks remain a national minority with their own religion and peculiarities, assimilation being only one of three equal options.

ban-cartels.rationale: The Aufbau and the 1940 proposals call for breaking up titanic enterprises and ending monopolies, but the 1925/26 programme told the economics ministry to combine similar works into cartels.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Strasser's 1940 programme says equal rights cannot be granted to the totalitarian parties of the Nazis or the Bolsheviks.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest remains obtainable under the Aufbau, at an official rate set by the Reichsbank, though mortgages on land and enterprises become impossible.

bound-labor.rationale: The Aufbau presents the entail as freeing the peasant from interest slavery and the junkers, making him a free and independent peasant who owes a tithe to the community, not labour to a lord.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Aufbau says capitalism is in the throes of a crisis from which no exit can be found and that its foundations will never again be firmly established.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Germany Tomorrow demands the independence of art from any State interference, though it would have a committee censor schoolbooks.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The Aufbau makes the Reichsbank a State institution that fixes interest rates as part of the planned economy.

central-planning.rationale: The Aufbau holds that a socialist economy is impossible without a planned economy, with systematically planned management of the whole national economy by the State, though enterprises keep their own managers and compete.

character-from-environment.rationale: The Aufbau holds that experience precludes any change in human nature and that people differ intrinsically in quality, education only fostering what is given.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The Aufbau replaces the patchwork of support with a unified national insurance guaranteeing every citizen a sufficiency, leaving only supplementary cover to voluntary choice.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The 1925/26 programme made the citizenship of Jews depend on descent, with the father deciding mixed cases; the later texts do not restate it.

civilizational-union.rationale: Germany Tomorrow calls the spirit of Christianity the bond of the West and wants its peoples, without Russia, joined in a European Federation.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Germany Tomorrow makes a European Colonial Company the guardian of Africa's indigenes until they develop, and the Czechs the instructors of the Ruthenians.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Aufbau's factory fellowship makes manager, staff and State partners in every enterprise, replacing the class of capitalists and the proletariat with estates.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Aufbau explains history by the swing between the conservative and liberal ideas and rejects Marxism's class-war tactics.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: German socialism replaces classes with vocational estates and rejects the class-war tactics of Marxism.

clerical-rule.rationale: The Aufbau favours separation of Church and State and keeps the State out of Church affairs, with power held by a president and estate chambers.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The 1925/26 programme claimed Austria, the Sudetenland and South Tyrol for a Greater German Reich, while the 1940 programme leaves such areas to their inhabitants' vote.

collective-defense.rationale: Germany Tomorrow makes collective security, with members pledged to resist together an attack on any member, the chief feature of the European Federation.

collective-farming.rationale: Agriculture under the Aufbau rests on individual hereditary farms held in 'entail', which it calls substantially individual in character, unlike the collective factory fellowships.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Germany Tomorrow treats colonies chiefly as a question of raw materials, investment and settlement for European States, while naming the company guardian of the indigenes.

common-currency.rationale: The Aufbau adds to Germany's own currency a supranational currency for the European economic area, and the 1940 proposals call for unified currency systems in the European Federation.

conscription.rationale: The Aufbau makes army service voluntary and Strasser's 1940 programme declares him absolutely opposed to universal military service, with a Swiss-style militia only as a fallback.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The Aufbau condemns daily needs artificially developed by advertisement and sets a thoughtful, cheerful existence against boundless production and consumption.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Aufbau holds that monopoly owners' economic power radiates into politics and that party government is spread by selfish groups of capitalists.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Vocational councils of workers, peasants, employees, traders and professions supervise wages and working conditions, and the Chambers of Estates take part in matters of prices.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The 1940 programme rejects ranking peoples as better or worse, yet calls some peoples advanced and others backward or semi-civilized.

death-penalty.rationale: The Aufbau's German law expiates all offences against the community by banishment or death.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The Aufbau demands a comprehensive national insurance covering childhood, unemployment, accident, old age and death, so that no member of the community goes hungry.

decide-locally.rationale: The Aufbau and the 1940 programme want a federation of provinces with the greatest possible self-government, and call a maximum of self-government the only safeguard against bureaucracy.

defeat-communism.rationale: Germany Tomorrow calls Bolshevism a deadly peril to be overcome and extirpated from Europe.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Germany Tomorrow wants Bolshevism extirpated from Europe, and the Aufbau calls the Soviet State the class rule of a bureaucracy.

democracy-best.rationale: The Aufbau calls popular government a gain-seeking falsehood of liberalism and replaces it with an 'authoritarian democracy' of estates, though it prefers parliamentary government to any uncontrolled dictatorship.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: The Aufbau condemns parties for sundering the people into factions and fostering oppositions, and makes their destruction the condition of a commonwealth.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Aufbau rejects the proletarian dictatorship as in practice the class rule of a bureaucracy, and the book rejects the class rule of the proletariat outright.

direct-action.rationale: The Aufbau's postface rejects any democratic choice or coalition with the old system and says a few self-sacrificing people, not the masses, will make the revolution.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The Aufbau has the Great Council elect the president of the Reich by simple majority rather than the people.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Germany Tomorrow calls for free plebiscites under international supervision in Austria, the Sudetenland (by district) and the Danzig region.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The Aufbau limits the acquisition of money by the work a man can do, so that the standard of life is as differentiated as human nature demands.

divinely-chosen-superior-people.rationale: Strasser's 1940 programme disavows any valuation of peoples as better or worse, since all have equal rights, needs and duties by the will of the Creator.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The Aufbau excludes hereditary succession to the headship of the State, since talent is not transmitted by inheritance.

economic-freedom.rationale: The Aufbau holds that the economic power of monopoly owners radiates into the political field as servitude, and that no freedom is possible under social and economic monopolies.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The Aufbau demands absolute national autarchy in food and relative autarchy otherwise, as a step towards European autarchy, with only a luxury trade beyond it.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The Aufbau warns against an overproduction of intellectuals and of people 'intellectualized' out of their healthy instincts in the big towns.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Aufbau excludes hereditary monarchy and has the head of state elected for life by the Great Council.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Germany Tomorrow wants a European Federation with arbitral powers and joint forces within a renovated League of Nations, starting from a minimum of coercion.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Germany Tomorrow commits members of the European Federation to combine against any attack on one of them.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Aufbau repudiates the democratic principle of equality and holds people unequal in value, while the 1940 programme promises equal rights to all human beings.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The Aufbau repudiates the democratic principle of equality and wants the standard of life as differentiated as human nature demands.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Aufbau defines a people by race, country and history, and the 1925/26 programme sought the racial union of all Germans in a Greater German Reich, though the 1940 text accepts national minorities.

experts-over-public.rationale: The Aufbau holds that a person can judge only what he knows from his own work, and has economic control elaborated by experts.

family-wage.rationale: The 1925/26 programme raised basic pay automatically with marriage and children, and the Aufbau sets the manager's share to cover his family's living costs.

farm-price-support.rationale: The Aufbau presents German socialism as the peasant's redeemer from mortgagees, bankers and tax-gatherers, cancelling farm mortgages and pooling the risk of crop failure; the 1925/26 programme channelled credit through supervised loan banks.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The Black Front warned in 1937 that a worldwide coalition would partition Germany after Hitler's war, and Germany Tomorrow argues against a plan to disintegrate Germany.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The Aufbau names the owner's privilege to sell his property to a foreign individual, corporation or State as fatal to a planned economy; under German socialism the means of production cannot be sold at all.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The Aufbau sets out a full design for German socialism as an architect's plan, though it allows the plan to bend to life and small banks to test new monetary theories.

free-public-college.rationale: The Aufbau demands that education at all schools be free, with books supplied, and the 1925/26 programme made attendance at every school including the university free of charge.

free-trade.rationale: The Aufbau declares worldwide free trade dead and seeks European autarchy, though the 1940 programme abolishes customs barriers inside Europe.

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: Germany Tomorrow holds that joint economic advantages, including the abolition of customs barriers, are the strongest cement of the European Federation.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The Aufbau holds that whoever owns the monopolies can dispose at will of the life and death of millions, which makes the dependent majority unfree.

government-encourage-intercultural-conta.rationale: Germany Tomorrow calls for cultural collaboration in the European Federation, an 'Olympiad of the mind', a European Academy and high schools teaching in foreign tongues.

gradual-change.rationale: Gregor Strasser's text in Germany Tomorrow rejects being 'social reformers' who plaster over capitalism's sores, and the Aufbau expects revolution.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Aufbau's president appoints ministers who are only advisers responsible to him, and the 1925/26 programme gave the president the declaration of war and peace.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The Aufbau's elementary school teaches German, history and knowledge of the homeland so the child grows up in the German cultural world before meeting alien cultures.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The Aufbau grounds national ownership of the land in its having been won and defended by the community, and roots the German tribes in their territories for ages.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Under the Aufbau the acquisition of money is limited by what work a man can do and by that alone, and Gregor Strasser's text in the book calls for valuation by achievement instead of by ownership.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The 1925/26 programme speaks of the causal tie between the economic liberation of German workers and the political liberation of the people, a tie Gregor Strasser's text in Germany Tomorrow repeats.

independent-unions.rationale: The Aufbau insists the vocational councils govern themselves with absolute independence of the State and any party, unlike the corporations of Fascist Italy and the soviets.

indirect-election.rationale: Under the Aufbau the provincial and Reich councils are elected indirectly by the councils below them, and the president by the Great Council.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The Aufbau fuses all private insurance companies into one national life insurance scheme tied to the Reichsbank, with a compulsory basic grade deducted from wages.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Strasser's 1940 programme recognises national minorities, including a Jewish national group, as groups with their own institutions and a minister.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The Aufbau calls the domination of the machine an unmitigated curse and wants de-urbanization and the break-up of giant enterprises, while keeping modern industry.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Black Front rejected the narrow confines of a party for a trained elite, and Strasser likened its loose structure to Freemasonry.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The Aufbau holds that no people can take over intact the State forms of another, since the State must originate out of each people's nature.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Strasser's 1940 programme says Zionism should be supported by all nation-conscious peoples as a genuine renovation of Judaism.

labour-priority-over-capital.rationale: Gregor Strasser's text in Germany Tomorrow holds that work is more than possession and achievement more than dividends, and the Aufbau ends the rule of capital over workers.

land-redistribution.rationale: The subdivision of the great landed estates into peasant farms is fundamental to the Aufbau, and the 1925/26 programme split estates over 1,000 Morgen into peasant holdings.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land belongs to the nation and is held in entail by those able to farm it; it reverts to the community for bad farming or when no son can carry it on.

land-value-tax.rationale: The peasant pays a single tithe-rent fixed by the area and quality of his land and no other taxes, but industry pays its own imposts, so land rent replaces taxes only in agriculture.

leader-cult.rationale: The Black Front manifesto contrasts Gregor Strasser with the 'Byzantine' party leadership that demanded worship from idolaters, and Hitler and I attacks Hitler's uniformity.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Gregor Strasser's text in Germany Tomorrow calls for a synthesis drawing nationalism from the bourgeoisie and socialism from the proletariat, bridging the two camps.

local-production.rationale: The 1925/26 programme set the principle of the shortest possible route from producer to consumer, and the Aufbau calls for decentralized industry and de-urbanization.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The Aufbau rejects communism and every party system, condemning even a single monopolist party as worse than many parties.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Aufbau calls a planned economy the precondition of German socialism and says the capitalist system can no longer feed, clothe and house the people, while keeping rivalry between enterprises inside the plan.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Black Front manifesto in Germany Tomorrow pledges itself to the dead who fell for German socialism and honours Gregor Strasser as its martyr.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The Aufbau rejects materialism and traces history to the alternation of the ideas of conservatism and liberalism.

maximum-personal-income.rationale: The Aufbau fixes maximum and minimum incomes only during the transition and afterwards sets no limit to acquisition beyond a man's working powers.

means-match-ends.rationale: The Aufbau holds that a system can only be overthrown with the tools of the coming system, and the 1936 postface excludes means that run counter to the movement's ideas.

military-organisation-revolutionary-part.rationale: Strasser's Kampfgemeinschaft revolutionärer Nationalsozialisten called itself a school of officers and non-commissioned officers of the German revolution.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The Aufbau joins 'aristocratic responsibility' in a life president and Great Council with 'German democracy' in elected estate chambers, calling the result authoritarian democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Aufbau says the principle of equality of opportunity condemns hereditary monarchy, since a supreme position assured by birth is self-condemned.

money-backed-by-precious-metals.rationale: The Aufbau calls the abandonment of the international gold standard an essential preliminary to autarchy and attacks gold's legal privilege over all other commodities.

moral-incentives.rationale: The Aufbau sets out to harness personal egoism, a necessary and useful part of human nature, for the general welfare, leaving the peasant's extra surplus tax-free.

more-religion-public.rationale: Germany Tomorrow says a lasting cure for Germany can only come from a religious revival and whole-hearted acceptance of Christianity.

multipolar-world.rationale: Germany Tomorrow wants an equipoise of Latins, Germans and Slavs so that no people dominates Europe, and a League of continental groups.

municipal-property.rationale: The Aufbau makes the whole nation, through the State, the sole owner of the means of production, with municipalities acting at most as trustees for the State.

nation-first.rationale: The Aufbau puts national autarchy and self-maintenance against other communities first, while the 1940 programme puts European collaboration and joint security at the centre.

national-church-status.rationale: The Aufbau's 1936 edition favours separating the main Church from the State to the benefit of all religious communities, though the 1925/26 programme had the State protect and promote the two Christian confessions.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Strasser's 1940 programme incorporates a Jewish national group with its own religion and peculiarities into New Germany, with a State Department of National Minorities.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Germany Tomorrow requires members of the European Federation to accept its arbitral powers and the Permanent Court of International Justice.

national-mission.rationale: The Aufbau holds that no people can take over the State forms of another, so Germany's system is not for export.

national-rebirth.rationale: Strasserism's German Revolution is to overcome the dying liberal epoch, and the Aufbau ends by naming its meaning the resurrection of the West.

national-resource-control.rationale: Raw materials beneath German soil are the property of the community and cannot be sold, least of all to foreigners, under the Aufbau.

national-self-determination.rationale: Germany Tomorrow proclaims the inalienable right of individuals and nations to self-determination as the first principle of the peace.

native-born-offices.rationale: Germany Tomorrow requires that all functionaries of a province, from president to postman, be natives of that province.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Aufbau rests on the conservative view that people are unequal in what they can do for the community and summons only the best and most efficient to lead.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Aufbau presents German socialism as equally remote from western capitalism and eastern bolshevism and as hostile to both.

no-central-bank.rationale: The Aufbau keeps a State Reichsbank that issues banknotes and sets the official rate of interest.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Germany Tomorrow offers to give up Heligoland, destroy the Siegfried Line and compromise on the Corridor to secure peace.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Aufbau elects the president for life so that he is independent of electors and popular favour, in a State without parties.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Aufbau demands the elimination of all parties and calls Hitler's single monopolist party still more evil and corrupt than multi-party rule.

open-borders.rationale: Strasser's 1940 programme ends passports and hindrances to movement within the European Federation, while the 1925/26 programme expelled recent immigrants.

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: The 1936 postface tells German socialists to work for the overthrow of the Hitler system with any and every means, and the Black Front called for armed revolt.

organic-representation.rationale: The Aufbau abolishes all political parties and builds popular representation on vocational councils and Chambers of Estates.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Aufbau replaces parliament with three equal wielders of authority, so no elected assembly is supreme.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: The Aufbau holds that whoever uses liberal weapons to defeat a liberal system will fail, and opposes any democratic choice.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Aufbau wants to free the energies of self-government and encourage political responsibility down to the lowest strata through elected councils in every district.

party-controls-media.rationale: Strasser's 1940 programme demands the independence of the press from any State interference or social monopolization, and the Aufbau demands press freedom with signed articles.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Aufbau's schools aim not to impart information but to educate Germans and form character.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: German socialism holds that true socialism is identical with true nationalism, in Gregor Strasser's words in the book, and seeks the incorporation of the working class into the nation.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Aufbau separates monopoly goods (land, raw materials, means of production), owned by the nation, from goods that can be multiplied at will, including houses, which stay private property.

physical-labour-duty.rationale: The Aufbau requires a year of labour service in which every young German of both sexes learns a handicraft.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The Aufbau calls the party system a lie spread by selfish groups of capitalists and calls discontent with a privileged officialdom fully justified.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Germany Tomorrow calls the war an ideological, almost religious 'war of religions' between force and voluntary collaboration.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Germany Tomorrow wants member States to accept the European Federation's arbitration, a joint army and unified currency, beginning with a minimum of centralization.

population-transfer.rationale: The 1925/26 programme expelled Jews who had immigrated since 1914, but Strasser's 1940 programme let every member of a minority choose freely between foreign status, minority status and assimilation.

positive-liberty.rationale: The Aufbau holds that only possessions of one's own give independence, quoting 'Property makes free', and Hitler and I says no man is free who is not economically independent.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Aufbau has children grow up in the German cultural world without diversion towards alien cultures, and roots the State in the peculiarities of the people.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The State takes the peasants' tithe in kind and puts it on the market as needed to regulate prices, and the transition brings official control of prices.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The Aufbau gives justice to State people's courts and defence to a national (later European) army, leaving no room for private providers.

production-for-use.rationale: The Aufbau describes the change as turning profit-making industry into socialist industry working for use instead of profit, while managers and workers still share in profits.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Aufbau says capitalist ownership of monopolies split the people into exploiters and exploited, yet German socialism keeps profit as the manager's reward for work.

property-franchise.rationale: The Aufbau gives the vote to those who work, organised by vocation, rather than to owners or taxpayers.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Aufbau repudiates the capitalist law that private property is sacred and calls the abolition of private property in land, raw materials and the means of production the main demand of German socialism.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The Aufbau holds that an unrestricted right to do what one likes with one's own conflicts with the vital interests of the people, and the holder of an entail must manage it for the best advantage of the community or lose it.

proportional-representation.rationale: The Aufbau unconditionally rejects any election by political parties and groups and replaces them with vocational elections.

public-ownership.rationale: The Aufbau makes the nation the sole owner of land, raw materials and the means of production, and the 1940 proposals add that monopolist industries must be nationalized.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The 1940 programme makes freedom of the spirit, belief and conscience a foundation of the New Germany, and the Aufbau proclaims freedom of faith and conscience.

race-social-construct.rationale: The Aufbau treats races as biological constituents of peoples, citing Günther's four or five primary races of Europe.

racial-franchise.rationale: The 1925/26 programme declared Jews foreigners without the vote or office, but Strasser's 1940 programme promises equal rights for all human beings and a minister for national minorities.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Aufbau rejects rationalism and materialism and humbly accepts God's will as the presupposition of all human action.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The 1925/26 programme expelled recent Jewish immigrants, but Strasser's 1940 programme opens the countries of the European Federation to each other's settlers.

refuse-to-join-illegitimate-government.rationale: The Aufbau's postface says the movement must ruthlessly oppose any participation in a coalition with the old system.

regional-resource-ownership.rationale: The Aufbau vests land and raw materials in the whole nation, not in the provinces where they lie.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Every large enterprise becomes a factory fellowship in which the State holds a third of possession, profits and control, ensuring permanent control of production, wages and prices.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Aufbau affirms the greatness and everlastingness of the religious sentiment uniting the soul with God.

religious-nation.rationale: The Aufbau forms the people from race, country and history, not religion, and separates Church and State, even while calling Christianity the bond of the West.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: The 1925/26 programme expelled Jews who had arrived since 1914, but Strasser's 1940 programme keeps minorities in Germany with equal rights.

replace-appointed-officials.rationale: The Aufbau appoints provincial presidents for seven years and circle presidents for five, and strips officials of security against dismissal.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Service in the vocational councils and Chambers of Estates is honorary under the Aufbau, with compensation for lost time but no financial advantage.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: The Aufbau asks revolutionaries to stake their lives, and the Black Front called Germans to arms against Hitler.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The Aufbau makes the nation the owner of the raw materials beneath the land and charges those who exploit them an impost to the community.

restore-past-order.rationale: The Aufbau calls its socialists akin to the forms of the Middle Ages, revives the Old-Germanic entail and the knight as ideal type, and names its aim the resurrection of the West.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The 1925/26 programme demanded the 1914 borders with the colonies, but the 1940 programme gives up Germany's colonial claim and leaves Danzig to self-determination.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The Aufbau's ideal is a re-agrarianized Germany of settled peasants and craftsmen, not a return to hunting and gathering.

return-to-pre-conversion-religion.rationale: The Aufbau calls any attempt to eliminate Christianity from the West foolish and impracticable, and Hitler and I records Strasser's objection to Rosenberg's paganism.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The 1925/26 programme demanded all Germans of Central Europe in one Greater German Reich, while the 1940 programme leaves Austria and the Sudetenland to free plebiscites.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Strasser's 1940 programme supports Zionism yet also lets Jews remain in Germany as a national minority, leaving each adult to choose.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Aufbau calls the huge towns a danger to the race and an abundance of settled peasants the best guarantee of public health and energy, and blames urban massing for weakening healthy instincts.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Aufbau calls the people an organism and the durable reality while the State is transient, and finds life's meaning in perfecting the people's soul as a revelation from God.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Aufbau rejects the demigod role dictators give the State and treats the head of state as an elected office.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Germany Tomorrow, true to its author's conservative principles, wants time-honoured institutions maintained and national customs preserved.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Aufbau's 1936 text is strongly in favour of separating Church and State; the 1925/26 programme had instead had the State protect and promote the Christian confessions.

separated-powers.rationale: The Aufbau divides State authority among a life president, a Great Council and a Reich Chamber of Estates with equal powers, any two needed to pass a law, and lets chambers veto officials.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The Aufbau holds that human nature cannot be changed and that one must not even try, and the 1940 programme makes human dignity the ground of equal rights.

simple-living.rationale: The Aufbau calls for simplifying life, says culture does not depend on luxury or advertised wants, and sets a thoughtful and cheerful existence above boundless consumption.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Germany Tomorrow calls for destroying the centralized Prussian administrative apparatus, and the Aufbau says a system cannot be overthrown with its own tools.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Gregor Strasser's text in Germany Tomorrow rejects the class rule of the proletariat as firmly as that of the bourgeoisie, and the Aufbau spreads power across five vocational estates.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The Aufbau builds German socialism on the German character and national autarchy, saying no people can adopt another's forms.

socialized-markets.rationale: Under the Aufbau the means of production belong to the nation and are held in fief, while enterprises keep a wholesome rivalry and ordinary commodities are freely bought and sold.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Germany Tomorrow demands that right, not might, prevail in each nation's domestic affairs and that member States be subject to the reign of law.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Aufbau rejects State capitalism, 'euphemistically termed State socialism', and says that under a bureaucracy there is no proletarian dictatorship but the rule of the official class, likening Russia's Stakhanov movement to early capitalism.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Aufbau holds that life is unified in body, mind and soul and that German socialism must serve all three, faulting liberalism and Marxism for materialism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Aufbau treats the State as the organizational form of the people, a tool fitted to the nation, and says even the capitalist State must stay fairly impartial between employer and worker.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Foreign trade follows a plan drafted to suit the needs of the State, and the State's third in every enterprise secures its lasting joint leadership of economic life.

state-finances-worker-businesses.rationale: The Aufbau encourages voluntary producers' cooperatives but rules out any material favouring of them by the State.

state-harmful.rationale: The Aufbau treats the State as the necessary organizational form of the people, rejecting only its idolization.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: The Aufbau has German education concentrate on producing a knightly, chivalrous ideal type as the nation's elite.

strong-leader.rationale: The Aufbau's life president holds a majority in the Great Council and predominant influence in the Reich Chamber, and the 1925/26 programme made the first president a dictator.

students-direct-own-learning.rationale: The Aufbau decides admission to university by the will of the community through teachers and examiners, not by what pupils want.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Aufbau wants the Churches freed from an unworthy dependence on the State, which should never interfere in their internal affairs.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Aufbau abolishes all political parties, but it also keeps the vocational councils free of the State and guarantees a free press, so organised opposition is curbed only in party form.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The 1925/26 programme demanded high protective tariffs, and the Aufbau shields the national (later European) economy behind a State monopoly of foreign trade and common external tariffs.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The Aufbau keeps a heavy inheritance tax as the only tax of the old kind, with strict legal control of inheritance; the 1925/26 programme had asked only for moderate inheritance-tax rates.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Aufbau grounds tithes and imposts in the duties every citizen owes the community, which owns the land and enterprises.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The Aufbau calls for ending the tyranny of technique and repudiates the overvaluing of technical acquirements.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The Aufbau uses long-distance power transmission and engines to decentralize industry while reviving Old-Germanic land tenure and the knightly ideal.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The 1925/26 programme demanded the 1914 borders and a central African colonial empire, but the Black Front later repudiated every kind of imperialism.

total-state.rationale: The Aufbau rejects with the utmost emphasis the principle of the totalitarian State and holds that the State can only regulate part of social life.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The Aufbau says fascists and communists rival one another in glorifying the State and suppressing independence, and the 1940 programme bars the totalitarian parties of Nazis and Bolsheviks alike.

unions-good.rationale: The Aufbau stresses what the Marxist labour movement achieved for the masses, especially the importance of the trade unions, though in German socialism unions become workers' cooperatives for vocational training.

universal-morality.rationale: The Aufbau says there is no law as such, since the sense of right derives from each people, while the 1940 programme appeals to the Law of God and moral laws giving all human beings equal rights.

vote-at-sixteen.rationale: The 1925/26 programme gave the vote in the vocational chambers at 21.

war-builds-character.rationale: Germany Tomorrow condemns Hitler's hysterical heroism and militarism as a malady, though Gregor Strasser's text in it praises volunteers for the heroic virtues of war.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Aufbau says owners of monopolies can dispose of the life and death of millions and that their economic power radiates as servitude into the political and cultural fields.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The Aufbau's main task is to deproletarianize Germans by giving every German possessions, with farms limited to what one man can work, though ownership itself stays with the nation.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: The Aufbau rejects the creed that man is sent into the world in order to work and treats labour as only a means of life.

worker-ownership.rationale: Workers hold only a share of possession and profits alongside the manager and the State, which remains the exclusive proprietor of every enterprise; the 1925/26 programme gave the staff 10 per cent of the shares.

workers-nation.rationale: German socialism calls Marxism alien for its internationalism and seeks the incorporation of the German working class into the nation.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Aufbau ends all political parties and represents workers through a workers' council among five vocational estates.

workplace-democracy.rationale: In the factory fellowship management, possession and profits fall in thirds to the manager, the staff and the State, and each worker can exert his possessive right on the supervisory council.

missingStatements.text: The state should hold ultimate ownership of all land and lease it to citizens on hereditary terms.
missingStatements.rationale: Central to the Fourteen Theses and Strasser Program: land held as inheritable state fiefs.

notes: Later pass (claude-opus-5-5, 2026-11-09) bringing the 2026-10-15 audit to rules 5, prompted by search traffic (closest ideology of Nick Fuentes). The first pass rested mostly on Wikipedia (s2, s3, s5, s6), on Hitler and I (s1) and on an Ossietzky review (s4) that could not be reopened; every answer was checked against Strasser's own programmes, now read in full: Germany Tomorrow (s7, containing the Aufbau and the Black Front manifestos) and the 1925/26 programme printed by Kühnl (s9), with Kühnl (s8), Gottfried (s10) and Hughes (s11) as scholarship. Answers resting only on the old sources were changed or nulled, the old version kept in reviewHistory. Strasserism never governed, so it has no record: every source is words. Strasser's positions changed: the 1925/26 draft demanded the 1914 borders, colonies, a 'national dictatorship', protective tariffs and the reclassification of Jews as foreigners without the vote, while the Aufbau (1931/1936) and the 1940 proposals reject the totalitarian State and imperialism, separate Church and State, open Europe to free trade and settlement and promise equal rights and minority status. Where the texts take opposite sides the answer is 0 at low confidence. Hughes (s11) argues that Strasser remained an antisemite and whitewashed his past, which the answers do not override since they follow the programmes' stated positions. Themes searched: economy (property, entail, factory fellowships, planning, money, taxes, insurance), government (estates, president, provinces, parties, officials), liberty (press, religion, punishment), means (revolution, violence, elections), society (race, minorities, Jews, schools, family), world (Versailles, Europe, colonies, disarmament, Bolshevism), technology and ecology (de-urbanization, machines). Not available: the 1929 Fourteen Theses of the German Revolution (only in the Lane and Rupp anthology, which was not found in a publisher's or library's open copy) and Strasser's post-war Der Faschismus and solidarism writings; Ossietzky's review (s4) was read in its original 1932 Weltbühne printing: it quotes the 1931 first edition of the Aufbau as stripping citizenship from a German who marries a member of another people and as denying Jews citizenship and fiefs, passages absent from the 1940 English text; since the 1931 edition could not be checked, these quotations are not used as evidence, but they show that the 1940 text's minority rights are a later change.
